hero.headline: Pulte Homes targets bargain hunters with new St. Lucie County development
hero.body:
Pulte Homes is developing new housing aimed at South Florida buyers looking for more affordable options in St. Lucie County. The national homebuilder is specifically marketing to residents seeking lower-priced homes compared to other parts of the region.

The development represents a shift in strategy for major builders who are targeting cost-conscious buyers in St. Lucie County. The county has become an increasingly attractive option for homebuyers priced out of other South Florida markets, with builders responding to demand for more affordable housing options.

Pulte Homes is one of the nation's largest homebuilders and has been active in Florida for decades. The company builds homes across multiple price points, but this St. Lucie County project specifically targets buyers seeking value in the current housing market.

The announcement comes as St. Lucie County continues to see residential growth, with Port St. Lucie and surrounding areas attracting both families and retirees looking for housing options more affordable than coastal markets in Palm Beach, Broward, and Miami-Dade counties.

cards.headline: One Person Airlifted After SUV-Semi Crash Closes I-95 Lanes in Martin County
cards.body:
A serious crash involving an SUV and a semi-truck on Interstate 95 in Martin County sent one person to the hospital by air ambulance with traumatic injuries. The crash occurred Thursday near Kanner Highway and shut down multiple lanes of the busy interstate corridor.

The collision between the SUV and semi-trailer closed all northbound lanes of I-95 near the Kanner Highway exit. The closure created significant traffic delays for commuters traveling through the Martin County stretch of the interstate, one of the main transportation arteries connecting the Treasure Coast to points north and south.

Emergency responders airlifted one person from the crash scene with traumatic injuries. Air ambulance transport is typically reserved for the most serious medical emergencies, suggesting the severity of the injuries sustained in the collision. The Florida Highway Patrol and Martin County Fire Rescue responded to the scene.

The crash is the second major incident to affect I-95 traffic in Martin County within a 24-hour period. Motorists should expect delays in the area as investigators work to determine the cause of the crash and clear the roadway.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie woman sentenced to 3 years in prison for running illegal med spa out of backyard shed
cards.teaser: Rosa Mena, 50, of Port St.
cards.body:
Rosa Mena, 50, of Port St. Lucie has been sentenced to three years in prison and five years of probation after operating an illegal medical spa out of a shed in her backyard. The case came to light in May 2025 when a victim reported partial facial paralysis after receiving Botox injections from Mena at the makeshift facility called Miracle Hand and Spa on the 5000 block of Northwest Coosa Drive.

The victim, who had been referred to the business by coworkers, received 62 units of Botox injections during a session at the shed. When she reported the paralysis to Mena, Mena refunded the $325 fee and asked the victim to return for a vitamin injection to reverse the problems. When the victim requested to see her medical license, Mena provided an altered phlebotomy certificate that had actually expired in February 2024. Mena also claimed to be a doctor from the Dominican Republic.

A search warrant executed at Mena's residence by Port St. Lucie Police, PSL Code Enforcement, the PSL Building Department, PSL Business Tax and the Florida Department of Health uncovered extensive evidence of the illegal operation. Detectives found medical beds, fat sculpting machines, laser hair removal equipment, laser liposuction machines and injection devices for fillers and Botox.

Mena was convicted on multiple charges including three counts of aggravated battery causing bodily harm, three counts of practicing medicine without an active license, one count of fraud for obtaining property worth $300 or more, one count of fraud for obtaining property under $20,000, and one count of using a two-way communication device to facilitate a felony. The case involved a multi-agency investigation that exposed the scope of the illegal medical procedures being performed in the residential backyard shed.

cards.headline: Activists Rally to Save Rare Deep-Sea Coral Reef Off Fort Pierce as Federal Decision Looms
cards.body:
Dozens of community members gathered at the Blake Library in Martin County to rally for the protection of the Oculina Bank, a rare deep-water coral reef located just off the coast of Fort Pierce. The reef is home to more than 2,000 marine species and is found nowhere else on Earth. Unlike most coral that needs shallow sunlight to survive, the Oculina Bank thrives in deep, dark waters hundreds of feet below the surface.

The gathering followed a vote by a federally appointed council to roll back longstanding protections for the reef. Two proposals would reopen parts of the reef to shrimp trawling, even though scientists say trawling destroyed as much as 90 percent of the reef before federal protections were put in place decades ago. Dr. Grant Gilmore, a scientist who previously dived the rare reef, told the crowd he is very concerned from an ecosystem point of view. He explained that fish need habitat and food, and the coral reef provides both. Removing that habitat means losing the fish.

Bob Zales, executive director of the Southeastern Fishing Association and a generational shrimper, believes reopening shrimping access to the Oculina Bank is essential for the struggling rock shrimp industry. Council data shows the rock shrimp industry has plummeted from over 700 trips per year in the mid-1990s to under 100 since 2010. The number of active rock shrimpers dropped from 144 in 1996 to less than 30, with just 12 active boats in 2018. Zales attributes the decline to high costs, competition from imported shrimp, and closures of previously open fishing areas.

The proposals followed a Trump executive order issued in April of 2025 that tasked eight regional councils nationwide to find ways to reinvigorate the fishing industries. Mark Perry, executive director of the Florida Oceanographic Society, joined Gilmore at the gathering to urge the public to help save the reef. Scientists warned reopening the reef could irreparably damage what little remains of a coral system that grows very slowly and has been there for a long time. Corals are in trouble worldwide, and Gilmore said we should not be destroying any more of them.

cards.headline: Florida Lawmakers Pass Property Tax Cut Proposal That Would Increase Homestead Exemption
cards.teaser: Florida lawmakers passed a property tax cut proposal Tuesday that would increase the homestead exemption from $50,000 to $250,000 over two years, but it needs approval from 60 percent of voters in November.
cards.body:
The measure would increase the homestead exemption from $50,000 to $250,000 over two years, with inflation adjustments beginning in 2029. The bill would also lower assessment caps on non-homesteaded properties from 10 percent to 5 percent. Local experts are divided on what the ripple effects could be for residents and local governments.

Real estate attorney Steve Wallace, based in Boynton Beach, raised the possibility of new fees tied to local services. Wallace said there could potentially be non-ad valorem taxes assigned to the sheriff's office, fire rescue, and other services. CPA Paul Miller suggested businesses could end up carrying more of the financial burden to offset lost revenue through fees on tax returns and other annual charges. Municipal attorney Raul Gastesi offered a different perspective, suggesting the measure could actually push home prices higher because home buyers would have more money at their disposal.

Danielle Blake, Chief of Residential Advocacy at MIAMI REALTORS + RWorld, was skeptical of that theory. Blake pointed to interest rates as a more significant barrier to sales than property taxes alone, noting that what is really holding back sales is the interest rates. All four experts acknowledged there are significant unknowns about how counties, municipalities and markets might respond to decreasing property tax revenue. As with any ballot measure that passes, lawmakers would need to return to Tallahassee to work out the specifics in a bill to implement the changes.

The schools police chief is responsible for overseeing security and law enforcement operations across all Martin County school campuses. This role includes managing school resource officers and ensuring the safety of students and staff throughout the district.

The arrest could have implications for the Martin County school district as administrators consider how to address the situation. School district officials will need to determine whether the police chief will remain in the position or if changes to the leadership structure of the school police department are necessary.

The merger and closure of middle schools will directly impact students currently attending the affected campuses, who will be reassigned to other facilities. Parents and families in the affected areas will need to adjust to new school assignments and potentially longer commutes for their children.

School consolidation efforts are often driven by enrollment changes, budget considerations, or the need to upgrade aging facilities. The split vote suggests that board members weighed competing priorities, including maintaining neighborhood schools versus achieving cost efficiencies or addressing capacity issues across the district.

cards.headline: Jupiter Island Officials Say Town is Prepared Despite Report Warning of 9 Feet of Flooding
cards.teaser: Jupiter Island leaders say they are ready for future storms following a new vulnerability assessment that identified 103 critical town assets at risk of flooding, including the Emergency Operations Center.
cards.body:
Jupiter Island Commissioner Marshall Field says town leaders were not surprised by a new Florida Department of Environmental Protection vulnerability assessment that warned 103 critical town assets face flood risk. The report identified 68 stormwater facilities, 17 historic sites, conservation lands, and key evacuation routes that could be threatened. The town's Emergency Operations Center could see up to 9 feet of floodwater, according to the report.

Field said the findings confirm what town leaders already knew, which is why they requested the assessment in the first place. The town's Beach District Director John Duchok explained the vulnerability assessment will set up the roadmap for how the town adapts and takes on the highest priorities first. The findings come on the heels of a separate state study warning that severe erosion could one day break through part of the island.

Field said evacuation orders would be issued well before floodwaters threaten roadways, and that the town has a backup facility on the mainland to maintain operations during emergencies. The town intends to compete for state and federal funding to fix vulnerabilities, with a funding window opening June 1. Field said the commission has a responsibility to utilize any and all state and federal resources available. The 126-page report also warns that stormwater systems face some of the greatest risks, noting they can fail during the very flooding events they are designed to manage.

cards.headline: 12 kids from Make-A-Wish Foundation sworn in as junior deputies at St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office
cards.teaser: Sheriff Richard Del Toro swore in 12 kids from the Make-A-Wish Foundation as junior deputies on Wednesday, calling it one of the greatest days in his career.
cards.body:
Among the newest junior deputies were twins Mia and Daryl Nyack. In 2023, Mia was diagnosed with aplastic anemia, a blood disorder, and needed a bone marrow transplant. Her twin brother Daryl donated his bone marrow to save his sister's life. Their mother Melissa Nyack said her son endured a lot of pain and was in a wheelchair during the process. Mia said she was scared, but her brother made her feel safe.

The junior deputies toured the sheriff's office, saw the helicopter, SWAT team, and K-9 demonstrations, and received badges. Another junior deputy, Tobias, was diagnosed with B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia in 2022. His mother Charity Deleon said things that do not normally happen to a child happened to him, and they even lost him at one point before he miraculously recovered.

Deleon thanked the sheriff's office for making the time and energy to welcome the children into the community and remind them that they are important. Sheriff Del Toro said the young heroes left an imprint on the law enforcement officers, adding that the kids made their wish come true.

cards.teaser: MorseLife has announced a multi-county expansion of its PACE program and behavioral health services, extending care options for seniors and residents needing mental health support.

MorseLife is expanding its PACE program and behavioral health services across multiple Florida counties. The expansion will bring additional healthcare options for seniors and residents requiring behavioral health services to a broader geographic area.

PACE, which stands for Program of All-Inclusive Care for the Elderly, provides comprehensive medical and social services to seniors who need nursing home level care but want to remain in their communities. The program coordinates all aspects of care, including primary care, hospital care, prescription drugs, and social services.

The behavioral health services expansion addresses growing mental health needs in Florida communities. MorseLife's multi-county approach aims to increase access to mental health care for residents who previously faced barriers to treatment due to geographic limitations or lack of local providers.

Vero Beach has a rich history dating back to the early 20th century, and recognizing the contributions of early settlers and community builders helps preserve that legacy. The historical marker will provide future generations with information about the pioneer's impact on the development of Vero Beach.

The closure represents the loss of a business with deep roots in the community. After 75 years, the shop has become part of local history, with many families shopping there across multiple generations for beach apparel and vacation clothing.

The announcement adds to a wave of longtime retail closures across Florida as small independent shops face challenges from online retail, changing consumer habits, and rising operational costs. The 75-year run makes this shop one of the longer-lasting independent retailers in Florida's competitive beach town markets.

The approval represents a significant step forward for the downtown revitalization effort, bringing new activity to a building that had been sitting vacant. The school will serve students in the Fort Pierce community once it opens its doors.

Downtown Fort Pierce has seen various redevelopment efforts in recent years, and the addition of an educational facility could bring increased foot traffic and activity to the area during school hours. The presence of a school downtown may also benefit nearby businesses and contribute to the ongoing transformation of the district.

The timeline for when the school will open and begin accepting students will depend on any necessary renovations or preparations required to convert the vacant building into a functioning educational facility. hero.headline: Lake Worth Beach to welcome paddlers completing 80-mile ocean crossing for cystic fibrosis families
hero.body:
More than 100 paddlers will cross 80 miles of open Atlantic Ocean this June in the annual Crossing for Cystic Fibrosis, launching from Bimini, Bahamas, at midnight on June 13 and arriving at Lake Worth Beach after 12 to 16 hours of paddling. The endurance event benefits the Pipers Angels Foundation, established by event founder Travis Suit in honor of his daughter Piper, who was diagnosed with cystic fibrosis at age 4. Spectators are invited to Lake Worth Beach on June 13 to cheer paddlers during a daylong beach celebration marking their arrival.

The crossing is part of a four-day schedule beginning June 10 with arrivals and a poolside social at Bimini Cove. Thursday brings a 4Ocean beach cleanup and community buffet dinner, followed Friday by a Paddle Out Rose Ceremony to honor cystic fibrosis warriors. Safety requirements are strict. All paddlers must wear U.S. Coast Guard-approved personal flotation devices, waterproof whistles, and reflective gear during dark hours. GPS trackers provided by the event must be worn and active at all times, and mandatory safety meetings will be held.

Participants from around the world are expected to join the fundraiser. Paddlers must raise at least $2,000 for the cause, while crew or virtual participants have a $500 minimum. Final contributions are due July 31. Suit, an avid paddler, created the event after learning about the natural respiratory benefits of ocean salt air for cystic fibrosis patients. The foundation provides direct support for patients and families, connecting them with resources and community.

Cystic fibrosis is a life-shortening genetic condition that affects the lungs and digestive system. High-profile community events like this one raise funds and spotlight ongoing needs for research, treatment, and family support. More information, registration, and donation details are available at crossingforcysticfibrosis.com and pipersangels.org.

cards.headline: Beetlejuice musical brings Broadway laughs to West Palm Beach through June 7
cards.teaser: The hit Broadway show Beetlejuice is playing at the Kravis Center through June 7, bringing the spooky Tim Burton story to life with humor and spectacle at the Alexander W. Dreyfoos Concert Hall.
cards.body:

The production features Ryan Stajmiger in the iconic striped suit playing the mischievous demon from Tim Burton's 1988 film. The show follows Lydia Deetz, a strange and unusual teen whose life changes after meeting two recently deceased neighbors and a demon with a flair for trouble. Stajmiger says he breaks the fourth wall frequently, communicating directly with the audience. During an early performance, his wig change went awry when both wigs came off at once, leaving him bald for an entire scene.

Performances include 7:30 p.m. shows on June 3 and June 4, 8 p.m. on June 5, matinee and evening performances on June 6, and a closing matinee on June 7. Tickets start at $34.50, available directly at kravis.org. The show is recommended for ages 13 and up with parental discretion advised.

The Kravis Center continues to draw major Broadway productions, offering Palm Beach County residents big-stage theatrical experiences and boosting the region as a cultural destination.

hero.headline: Florida Supreme Court upholds gas utility rate hike affecting customers statewide
hero.body:
The Florida Supreme Court has upheld a rate hike by a gas utility, a decision that impacts customers across the state. The ruling allows the utility to proceed with increased rates that will affect household and business energy costs for Floridians.

The case reached the state's highest court after challenges to the rate increase. The Supreme Court's decision Thursday resolves the legal challenge and confirms the utility's authority to implement the higher rates. Gas utilities in Florida serve millions of customers, making rate decisions significant for household budgets and business operating costs throughout the state.

Rate hikes by utilities typically follow requests to state regulators to recover infrastructure costs, maintenance expenses, or other operational investments. When approved, these increases translate directly to higher monthly bills for residential and commercial customers. The Florida Supreme Court's role in this case was to review whether the rate hike was legally sound under state law and regulatory standards.

The decision represents a significant development in Florida's ongoing regulation of utility costs. With the Supreme Court's ruling now final, the gas utility can move forward with implementing the approved rate structure. Florida households and businesses served by the utility should expect to see the rate changes reflected in upcoming billing cycles. The new ordinance updates Tampa's city code to permit camera enforcement in school zones, with violators facing $100 fines. The dramatic number of speeders captured in the initial test period underscores the safety concerns around schools and suggests the cameras could generate significant enforcement activity once fully deployed across all 18 planned locations.

Automated speed enforcement has become increasingly common in Florida cities seeking to improve safety in school zones without requiring constant police presence. The cameras photograph vehicles exceeding posted speed limits and citations are mailed to registered owners. The Tampa program joins similar initiatives in other Florida communities aimed at protecting students and pedestrians near schools.

cards.headline: Florida researchers find trees reduce storm wind force on buildings by up to 50 percent
cards.teaser: A Florida International University study demonstrates that strategic tree placement can significantly protect homes during storms.
cards.body:
Researchers at Florida International University have found that trees positioned around buildings can reduce wind force on structures by as much as 50 percent during storms. The findings come from testing conducted at the university's Wall of Wind facility, which simulates hurricane conditions.

The study examined how trees surrounding a low-rise building affected wind forces on different segments of the structure. The research showed that trees can serve as an effective natural barrier, substantially decreasing the impact of high winds on homes and other buildings. For a state regularly threatened by hurricanes and tropical storms, the findings offer valuable insight into natural storm protection methods.

The research has practical implications for Florida homeowners, urban planners, and building codes. Strategic landscaping with appropriate tree species and placement could provide meaningful storm protection while offering additional benefits like shade and property value enhancement. The Wall of Wind facility at Florida International University allows researchers to study real-world storm conditions in a controlled environment, making it a valuable resource for understanding how to better protect Florida structures from severe weather.

The collision between the SUV and semi-trailer closed all northbound lanes of I-95 near the Kanner Highway exit. The closure created significant traffic delays for commuters traveling through the Martin County stretch of the interstate, one of the main transportation arteries connecting the Treasure Coast to points north and south.

Emergency responders airlifted one person from the crash scene with traumatic injuries. Air ambulance transport is typically reserved for the most serious medical emergencies, suggesting the severity of the injuries sustained in the collision. The Florida Highway Patrol and Martin County Fire Rescue responded to the scene.

The crash is the second major incident to affect I-95 traffic in Martin County within a 24-hour period. Motorists should expect delays in the area as investigators work to determine the cause of the crash and clear the roadway.

cards.headline: Jupiter Island Emergency Operations Center Could Face 9 Feet of Flooding, State Report Warns
cards.teaser: Jupiter Island officials say they are prepared for storm threats despite a new state assessment warning that 103 critical town facilities face flood risks, including the Emergency Operations Center.
cards.body:
A new vulnerability assessment by the Florida Department of Environmental Protection identified 103 critical Jupiter Island assets at risk of flooding, including the town's Emergency Operations Center, which could see up to 9 feet of floodwater during major storms. The report also flagged 68 stormwater facilities, 17 historic sites, conservation lands, and key evacuation routes as vulnerable to flooding.

Jupiter Island Commissioner Marshall Field told investigators the findings confirm what town leaders already knew when they requested the assessment. The town's Beach District Director John Duchok said the vulnerability study will create a roadmap to prioritize improvements and compete for state and federal funding. Field emphasized that evacuation orders would be issued well before floodwaters threaten roadways, and the town maintains a backup facility on the mainland for emergency operations.

The findings come after a separate state study warned that severe erosion could one day split the island. Field said the town has a window opening June 1 to apply for state and federal funding to address vulnerabilities. The 126-page report also warned that stormwater systems face some of the greatest risks because they can fail during the very flooding events they are designed to manage.

cards.headline: Activists Rally at Martin County Library to Save Rare Deep-Sea Coral Reef Off Fort Pierce
cards.teaser: Dozens gathered at Blake Library after a federal council voted to roll back protections for the Oculina Bank, a rare deep-water coral reef found nowhere else on Earth.
cards.body:
Dozens of community members gathered at the Blake Library in Martin County to oppose proposals that would reopen parts of the Oculina Bank to shrimp trawling. The rare deep-water coral reef, located just off the coast of Fort Pierce, thrives hundreds of feet below the surface in deep, dark waters and is home to more than 2,000 marine species.

Dr. Grant Gilmore and Mark Perry, Executive Director of the Florida Oceanographic Society, were among the scientists urging the public to help save the reef. Scientists say trawling destroyed as much as 90 percent of the reef before federal protections were put in place decades ago. The proposals to reopen shrimping access followed a Trump Executive order issued in April 2025 that tasked eight regional councils nationwide to find ways to reinvigorate fishing industries.

Bob Zales, executive director of the Southeastern Fishing Association, argues that reopening access is essential for the struggling rock shrimp industry, which has plummeted from over 700 trips per year in the mid-1990s to under 100 since 2010. Council data shows the number of active rock shrimpers dropped from 144 in 1996 to less than 30, with just 12 active boats in 2018. The federal agency is preparing a final ruling on the protections.

cards.body:

Martin County's beaches face ongoing challenges from erosion and storm damage, making restoration projects critical for protecting both the natural environment and the communities that depend on beach tourism. The national recognition signals that the restoration techniques and approaches used in Martin County are being viewed as models for other coastal communities facing similar challenges.

The award comes as coastal communities across Florida continue to grapple with erosion and the long-term impacts of storms on beach systems. The project reflects ongoing development and population growth pressures in Martin County, where expanding and modernizing utility infrastructure remains essential to supporting residential and commercial needs. cards.headline: Nuclear Power Plant to Test 91 Emergency Sirens on June 4
cards.teaser: Residents will hear emergency sirens on Wednesday as a Florida nuclear power plant conducts its routine safety test.
cards.body:
A nuclear power plant in Florida will test 91 emergency warning sirens on June 4. The routine test is part of the regular safety and emergency preparedness protocols required for nuclear facilities.

The sirens are designed to alert residents living near the nuclear plant in the event of an emergency requiring evacuation or sheltering in place. These tests are conducted regularly to ensure all sirens are functioning properly and can reach the surrounding communities if needed.

Residents who hear the sirens during the test should understand that the test is routine and does not indicate any actual emergency. Nuclear power plants are required by federal regulations to maintain and regularly test their emergency warning systems as part of comprehensive safety plans.

cards.headline: Heiress Buying 8 Acres in Florida to Preserve Land From Development
cards.teaser: An heiress is purchasing 8 acres of Florida land with plans to preserve it and block future development.
cards.body:
An heiress has purchased 8 acres of land in Florida with the intention of preserving it from development. The purchase represents a growing trend of conservation-minded buyers acquiring property specifically to protect natural areas from future building projects.

The land acquisition comes as development pressure continues across Florida, where rapid population growth has led to concerns about the loss of natural areas and wildlife habitat. Private land purchases for conservation purposes have become an increasingly common strategy for protecting environmentally sensitive or historically significant properties that might otherwise be developed.

Conservation easements and private land preservation efforts supplement public land acquisition programs and help protect green spaces, wildlife corridors, and natural areas that contribute to regional environmental health and quality of life for residents.

hero.headline: Twelve children with Make-A-Wish sworn in as junior deputies at St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office
hero.teaser: Twelve kids from the Make-A-Wish Foundation were honored by the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office when Sheriff Richard Del Toro swore them in as junior deputies.
hero.body:
Sheriff Richard Del Toro of the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office swore in twelve children from the Make-A-Wish Foundation as junior deputies on Wednesday. Del Toro called it one of the greatest days in his career. The young heroes received badges, toured the sheriff's office, and witnessed demonstrations from the helicopter, SWAT team and K-9 units.

Among the newest junior deputies were twins Mia and Daryl Nyack. In 2023, Mia was diagnosed with aplastic anemia, a blood disorder that required a bone marrow transplant. Her twin brother Daryl donated his bone marrow to save his sister's life, enduring significant pain and time in a wheelchair. Mia said her brother made her feel safe during the frightening experience.

Another junior deputy, Tobias Deleon, was diagnosed with B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia in 2022. His mother Charity Deleon said her son experienced complications that don't normally happen to children, and at one point they lost him before medical staff were able to bring him back. She expressed gratitude to the sheriff's office for making her son feel important and welcomed in the community. Sheriff Del Toro said the children left an imprint on his department, adding that the kids made the sheriff's office's wish come true.

cards.headline: Pulte Homes acquires 50 acres in Fort Pierce for Vela Cove development
cards.teaser: Pulte Homes has purchased a 50-acre site in Fort Pierce for a new residential development called Vela Cove, targeting bargain hunters in South Florida.
cards.body:
Pulte Homes has acquired a 50-acre property in Fort Pierce for a residential development called Vela Cove. The major homebuilder is targeting South Florida buyers looking for more affordable housing options by developing homes in St. Lucie County, where prices remain lower than in more expensive coastal markets to the south.

The Fort Pierce location positions Pulte to tap into demand from buyers priced out of higher-cost areas while still offering relative proximity to employment centers and amenities in the region. St. Lucie County has seen increased development interest as homebuilders look for land to meet housing demand at price points more accessible to a broader range of buyers.

The Vela Cove project represents the latest in a series of residential developments moving forward in St. Lucie County as the area continues to grow. The development will add to the housing stock in Fort Pierce and contribute to the ongoing expansion of the county's residential footprint.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County considers rocket recovery facility at Port of Fort Pierce
cards.teaser: St. Lucie County officials are considering plans for a rocket recovery facility at the Port of Fort Pierce, which could bring aerospace industry operations to the area.
cards.body:
St. Lucie County is exploring the possibility of establishing a rocket recovery facility at the Port of Fort Pierce. The proposal would bring aerospace industry operations to the local port, potentially creating new jobs and economic activity in the Fort Pierce area.

The facility would be designed to support rocket recovery operations, taking advantage of the port's waterfront location and existing infrastructure. As the commercial space industry continues to expand in Florida, communities along the coast are looking at ways to participate in the growing sector beyond traditional launch operations at Cape Canaveral.

The consideration of a rocket recovery facility represents a potential diversification of economic activity at the Port of Fort Pierce. County officials are examining the feasibility and requirements for such a facility as they weigh the proposal's impact on the local economy and port operations.

cards.headline: Senator Ashley Moody honors Port St. Lucie Sgt. Levasseur with Florida's Finest Award
cards.teaser: Senator Ashley Moody presented Port St. Lucie Sergeant Levasseur with Florida's Finest Award in recognition of outstanding law enforcement service.
cards.body:
Senator Ashley Moody honored Port St. Lucie Sergeant Levasseur with the Florida's Finest Award, recognizing exceptional service in law enforcement. The award highlights outstanding work by law enforcement officers who demonstrate dedication to their communities and exemplary performance in their duties.

Sgt. Levasseur serves with the Port St. Lucie Police Department and received the recognition for contributions to public safety in the community. The Florida's Finest Award program acknowledges law enforcement officers across the state who go above and beyond in serving their communities.

The honor brings recognition to both Sgt. Levasseur and the Port St. Lucie Police Department, highlighting the professional standards maintained by local law enforcement. The award ceremony underscores the state's commitment to recognizing exceptional police work in communities throughout Florida.

cards.headline: Three arrested overnight in Port St. Lucie patrols for shoplifting and DUI
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie police arrested three people overnight during patrols, with charges ranging from shoplifting to driving under the influence.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie police made three arrests during overnight patrols, taking suspects into custody on charges including shoplifting and driving under the influence. The arrests came as officers conducted routine patrols throughout the city, responding to incidents and enforcing traffic laws.

The overnight arrests reflect ongoing law enforcement efforts to maintain public safety in Port St. Lucie. Police regularly conduct patrols during late night and early morning hours when certain types of criminal activity tend to increase.

The arrests demonstrate the Port St. Lucie Police Department's commitment to addressing both property crimes like shoplifting and dangerous behaviors such as impaired driving. Officers continue to patrol neighborhoods and commercial areas throughout the city to deter crime and respond to incidents as they occur.

cards.headline: Funeral arrangements announced for St. Lucie County firefighter Connor Whitehead
cards.teaser: Funeral arrangements have been announced for St. Lucie County firefighter Connor Whitehead, honoring his service to the community.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County fire service community is preparing to honor firefighter Connor Whitehead as funeral arrangements have been announced. Whitehead served as a firefighter in St. Lucie County, dedicating his career to protecting residents and responding to emergencies throughout the area.

The announcement of funeral arrangements allows the community, fellow firefighters, and residents to pay their respects and honor Whitehead's service. Fire departments across the region often come together to support one another during the loss of a fellow firefighter, recognizing the brotherhood and sacrifice inherent in the profession.

The upcoming funeral services will provide an opportunity for the St. Lucie County community to remember Whitehead's contributions and express gratitude for his service. The loss of a firefighter affects not only department colleagues but also the broader community that relied on his dedication and bravery.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie woman sentenced to 3 years in prison for running illegal med spa out of backyard shed
cards.teaser: Rosa Mena, 50, of Port St.
cards.body:
Rosa Mena, 50, of Port St. Lucie has been sentenced to three years in prison and five years of probation after operating an illegal medical spa out of a shed in her backyard. The case came to light in May 2025 when a victim reported partial facial paralysis after receiving Botox injections from Mena at the makeshift facility called Miracle Hand and Spa on the 5000 block of Northwest Coosa Drive.

The victim, who had been referred to the business by coworkers, received 62 units of Botox injections during a session at the shed. When she reported the paralysis to Mena, Mena refunded the $325 fee and asked the victim to return for a vitamin injection to reverse the problems. When the victim requested to see her medical license, Mena provided an altered phlebotomy certificate that had actually expired in February 2024. Mena also claimed to be a doctor from the Dominican Republic.

A search warrant executed at Mena's residence by Port St. Lucie Police, PSL Code Enforcement, the PSL Building Department, PSL Business Tax and the Florida Department of Health uncovered extensive evidence of the illegal operation. Detectives found medical beds, fat sculpting machines, laser hair removal equipment, laser liposuction machines and injection devices for fillers and Botox.

Mena was convicted on multiple charges including three counts of aggravated battery causing bodily harm, three counts of practicing medicine without an active license, one count of fraud for obtaining property worth $300 or more, one count of fraud for obtaining property under $20,000, and one count of using a two-way communication device to facilitate a felony. The case involved a multi-agency investigation that exposed the scope of the illegal medical procedures being performed in the residential backyard shed.

hero.headline: Indian River Mall demolition underway in Vero Beach area
hero.body:
Demolition crews have begun tearing down the Indian River Mall, bringing an end to a structure that has been part of the local landscape for decades. The demolition work is now actively in progress, marking a significant change to the commercial corridor in Indian River County.

The mall closure and subsequent demolition has stirred memories among longtime residents who shopped and spent time at the facility over the years. The site has been a gathering place and retail destination for the community, and its removal represents a major shift in the local retail landscape.

According to those involved in the project, the demolition satisfies multiple interests in the community. The mall had been struggling in recent years as retail patterns shifted, and the property is being cleared for potential redevelopment that could bring new economic activity to the area.

The demolition process will continue in the coming weeks as crews work to fully clear the site. Local officials and developers will need to determine the future use of the property, which occupies a prominent location in Indian River County.

cards.headline: Ultraluxury apartments at The Vivien on Indian River Boulevard begin welcoming residents
cards.teaser: The Vivien, a new upscale apartment community on Indian River Boulevard, has started filling its units with residents as the development opens.
cards.body:
The Vivien apartment complex on Indian River Boulevard has begun accepting residents into its ultraluxury units. The development represents a new tier of high-end residential options in the Vero Beach area, targeting renters seeking premium amenities and waterfront location.

The project adds significant new housing inventory to the Indian River County market, particularly at the upper end of the rental spectrum. Indian River Boulevard is one of the most desirable addresses in the area, running parallel to the Indian River Lagoon and offering water views.

The opening of The Vivien reflects continued investment in residential real estate along the Treasure Coast. As the apartments fill, the development will bring new residents to the area and contribute to the local housing mix in a market that has seen strong demand for quality rental properties.

cards.headline: Indian River County family of five receives fully furnished home from nonprofits
cards.teaser: A local family with three children has been given a newly furnished home thanks to the work of area nonprofit organizations.
cards.body:
A family of five in Indian River County has received a fully furnished home through the efforts of local nonprofit groups. The family now has a complete living space with all the furnishings needed to settle in immediately, from beds and kitchen appliances to everyday household items.

The donation represents a significant investment by the charitable organizations involved, who coordinated to provide not just shelter but a move-in ready home. Such comprehensive assistance can be transformative for families working to achieve stability, eliminating the financial burden of furnishing an entire household.

Community nonprofit partnerships like this one demonstrate the strength of local charitable networks in Indian River County. The organizations worked together to ensure the family had everything needed to create a comfortable home environment for the parents and their three children.

cards.headline: Vero Beach Air Show coordinated massive security operation
cards.teaser: The recent Vero Beach Air Show required an extensive and carefully coordinated security effort to protect attendees and performers.
cards.body:
The Vero Beach Air Show relied on a large-scale security operation involving multiple agencies and careful planning. The event required coordination among law enforcement, emergency services, and security personnel to manage crowds and ensure public safety during the aerial performances.

Air shows present unique security challenges because they combine large public gatherings with aircraft operations and require protection of both ground attendees and airspace. The security teams had to manage everything from crowd control to emergency medical response readiness while coordinating with pilots and air traffic protocols.

The successful execution of the security plan allowed the air show to proceed safely for spectators and performers. Such events require months of advance planning and bring together local police, fire departments, emergency medical services, and specialized security personnel to create a comprehensive safety network.

cards.headline: Vero Beach pioneer to be honored with Florida Historical Marker
cards.teaser: A significant figure in Vero Beach history will be commemorated with an official state historical marker recognizing their contributions to the community.
cards.body:
A Vero Beach pioneer will receive recognition through the placement of a Florida Historical Marker, honoring their role in the development of the community. The state historical marker program identifies and commemorates people, places, and events that shaped Florida history and local community development.

Historical markers serve as permanent reminders of the individuals who built and shaped communities across the state. They provide residents and visitors with context about local history and help preserve the memory of those who contributed to the area's growth and character.

The marker will become part of the network of historical designations throughout Indian River County that tell the story of the region's development. Such recognition helps current and future generations understand the roots of their community and the people who established Vero Beach as a settlement and helped it grow into the city it is today.

cards.headline: Free Hot Pink concert scheduled Friday at Riverview Park in Sebastian
cards.teaser: Sebastian residents can enjoy a free concert at Riverview Park on Friday evening featuring the band Hot Pink.
cards.body:
A free concert featuring Hot Pink will take place Friday at Riverview Park in Sebastian. The performance is open to the public at no charge, offering an evening of live music in one of the city's popular outdoor venues.

Riverview Park serves as a regular gathering spot for community events in Sebastian, providing waterfront views and open space for concerts and festivals. Free community concerts like this one give residents opportunities for entertainment and socializing without cost barriers.

The Friday evening timing makes the concert accessible for families and working residents. Such community events help build neighborhood connections and provide recreational options for Sebastian residents looking for local activities.

cards.headline: WWII veteran Bill Keegan celebrates 102nd birthday in Indian River County
cards.teaser: Bill Keegan, a World War II veteran living in Indian River County, has reached the remarkable milestone of 102 years.
cards.body:
Bill Keegan, a veteran of World War II, recently celebrated his 102nd birthday in Indian River County. Keegan is among the dwindling number of veterans who served during the Second World War and are still living to share their experiences and memories.

World War II veterans are now in their late 90s and beyond, making each birthday a significant milestone. The generation that fought in the war is aging, and communities across the country recognize the importance of honoring these veterans while they are still alive to receive recognition for their service.

Indian River County is home to numerous veterans from various conflicts, with the area's climate and communities making it a popular retirement destination for former military members. Keegan's longevity represents both personal resilience and the chance for younger generations to maintain a living connection to World War II history.
